:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/worked-solution:
The numerator and denominator are $u(x) = x$ and $v(x) = 9x^2 + 5x,$ respectively. Their derivatives are given by

 

$$
\begin{aligned}{u}^{′}(x) & =1, \\ {v}^{′}(x) & =18x+5.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the quotient rule, we have

$$
\eqalign{
			f'(x) 	& = \dfrac {u'(x)\cdot v(x) - u(x) v'(x)} {[v(x)]^2}\
				& = \dfrac{\left( 9x^2+5x \right )\cdot 1 -x\cdot \left( 18x+5 \right)}{\left( 9x^2+5x\right)^2}\
				& = \dfrac{\left( 9x^2+5x-18x^2-5x \right)}{\left( 9x^2+5x\right)^2}\
				& = -\dfrac{9x^2}{\left( 9x^2+5x\right)^2}.
		}
$$

Differentiating a Quotient Containing Other Functions

:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/worked-solution:
Let $u=1$ and $v=3x+7.$ Then

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} & =0\,\text{and}\,\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=3.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the quotient rule, we get

$$
\eqalign{
			\dfrac{\textrm{d}y}{\textrm{d}x}	& = \dfrac{ v\dfrac{\textrm{d}u}{\textrm{d}x}-u\dfrac{\textrm{d}v}{\textrm{d}x}}{v^2}\
										& = \dfrac{ \left( 3x+7 \right ) \cdot 0 -1\cdot 3}{\left( 3x+7\right)^2}\
										& = -\dfrac{3}{\left( 3x+7\right)^2}.
		}
$$
